system.name: service mesh (background)
system.one_liner: background diagram of a common Kubernetes service mesh where sidecar proxies and an ingress gateway route external traffic to backend pods

components.name: External router
components.role: routes external client traffic toward the service mesh

components.name: Ingress gateway
components.role: primary entry point that inspects packets, matches services, and load-balances to endpoint pods

components.name: Service mesh
components.role: groups the services and sidecars managed as one mesh

components.name: Service A
components.role: a service abstraction over a set of pods running the same application

components.name: Service B
components.role: a second service abstraction over its own set of pods

components.name: Sidecar
components.role: proxy sharing the pod's namespace that intercepts the app container's packets

components.name: Node (server)
components.role: a physical/virtual server hosting the ingress gateway and/or application pods

components.name: Pod
components.role: management unit packaging an app container with its sidecar; annotated with circuit-breaking or retry settings

components.name: Request routing / traffic management
components.role: ingress gateway logic that selects an endpoint pod and applies traffic-management features

components.name: Virtual switch
components.role: root-namespace switch that all pods on a node attach to for packet forwarding

components.name: Network interface card (NIC)
components.role: physical interface through which inter-node packets are sent and received

flows.what: external traffic entering the service mesh (blue)
Path 1: incoming packet traverses the virtual switch and network-stack operations at both the root and gateway namespaces
Path 2: gateway forwards the packet back through the virtual switch to the selected endpoint pod
upstream connection to a locally selected endpoint pod (green arrow)
packet encapsulated and forwarded via the NIC when the endpoint pod is on a different node (orange, inter-node path)

content.key_idea: A generic service mesh places sidecars alongside app containers and routes all external traffic through an ingress gateway, whose packet analysis and forwarding path traverses a virtual switch and network stack twice, once at the root namespace and once at the destination pod's namespace.
content.reading_order: Top: client to external router to ingress gateway into the service mesh's services/sidecars. Bottom: two peer nodes, each a stack of gateway/pod, virtual switch, and NIC, linked by inter- and intra-node paths.

summary: Figure 1 is a background diagram (not HybridMesh itself) explaining how a typical Kubernetes service mesh is structured. External clients reach the mesh through an external router and an ingress gateway, which inspects L7 packet headers and payloads to match a destination service and select an endpoint pod, then forwards packets over an upstream connection (green arrow) or, if the pod is on another node, an inter-node path through the NIC (orange arrow). Each service groups pods that pair an app container with a sidecar proxy in the same namespace. The bottom half shows two peer nodes, each drawn as a stack of gateway/pod, virtual switch, and network interface card, illustrating the complex forwarding path (Path 1, Path 2) that repeatedly crosses the virtual switch and network stack. A bottom legend distinguishes connection, external, inter-node, and intra-node traffic.
summary_zh: 图1为背景图，展示典型Kubernetes服务网格：客户端经外部路由器到入口网关，网关解析流量后经上行连接或跨节点路径转发到目标Pod；每个节点内网关/Pod、虚拟交换机、网卡分层堆叠，体现复杂的转发路径。
notes: layout-proposal: twin-node layered network stack — two side-by-side peer nodes, each a vertical stack (gateway/pod, virtual switch, NIC), linked by inter-/intra-node paths and fed from a shared client-to-gateway chain above; no single named template captures both the top pipeline and the mirrored per-node layering.
